quickfire.question: What distinguishes a circular linked list from a singly linked list?
options: The last node's next pointer points back to the head
Nodes are allocated in contiguous memory
The head node stores the list size
quickfire.answer: The last node's next pointer points back to the head

routineWriter.questionText: Write the makeCircular routine that takes a tail node and a head node and closes the circular link.

commonMistakes.description: The only change needed — tail->next = NULL would leave it as a regular singly linked list

quickfire.question: Why must circular list traversal use a do-while loop rather than a regular while loop?
options: while loops don't support pointer arithmetic
A while loop checking curr != head would never enter if starting from head
do-while is faster for pointer-based structures
The compiler requires do-while for cyclic data
quickfire.answer: A while loop checking curr != head would never enter if starting from head

routineWriter.questionText: Write traverseOnce — visit every node exactly once in a circular linked list, starting from head.

commonMistakes.description: Must be do-while — a while (curr != head) check before visiting skips head entirely
Termination condition is curr == head (back to start), not curr == NULL (which never happens)
